title: COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT PROCESSES IN THE ECONOMIES OF UZBEKISTAN AND AZERBAIJAN
summary: This article presents a comparative analysis of business development processes and the formation of the entrepreneurial environment in the economies of Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan. The study examines mechanisms for supporting small businesses and private entrepreneurship, investment climate, tax policy, digital economy, export potential, and the impact of economic reforms on business development in both countries. In addition, the role of business activity in economic growth, employment, and regional development is evaluated based on statistical indicators. As a result of the research, scientific and practical recommendations aimed at improving the business environment were developed based on the experiences of Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan.

title: Assessing the impacts of solid waste management in the context of corporate social responsibility and the circular economy
summary: Growing solid waste generation creates public health and environmental challenges, highlighting the need for integrated waste management approaches that support a clean environment and society. This study assesses and develops a framework describing how solid waste management methods influence environmental sustainability and public health outcomes, while observing the role of corporate social responsibility (CSR). This study adopted a quantitative research design to evaluate the relations among solid waste management practices, environmental impacts, health outcomes, circular economy and CSR using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Data collection was completed through a structured questionnaire administered to 200 respondents. The questionnaire was developed based on the theoretical foundations of waste hierarchy, circular economy, and sustainable waste management. Considering the importance of the waste hierarchy and circular economy parameters, this study categorizes solid waste management as segregation, recycling, composting, and disposal methods. The analysis of the conducted study advocates the impact of the environment as an indicator to connect waste management practices and health outcomes. The results show that solid waste management methods meaningfully improve environmental sustainability when the strategies such as segregation, recycling, and composting are followed, as they contribute to current resource recovery and waste reduction. The finding further proposes that sustainable waste management aids to the quality of life and public health by reducing environmental hazards. Furthermore, it envisioned corporate social responsibility as a better tool to implement waste management approaches, with the enhanced stakeholder’s engagement and organizational responsibility. This study further elaborates to investigate sustainability by incorporating CSR, circular economy, waste hierarchy, public health, and environmental quality within an integrated analytical framework. The practical solutions are recommended to organizations and policymakers for developing and implementing sustainable waste governance.

title: Dual-Policy Coverage and Corporate Green Innovation: Evidence from China’s Commercial Logistics Node City Program and Supply Chain Innovation and Application Pilot Program
summary: Logistics network development and supply chain organizational innovation may create external conditions for corporate green innovation. Using 30,700 firm-year observations for Chinese A-share listed companies from 2012 to 2024, this study examines the relationship between joint coverage by the Commercial Logistics Node City Program and the Supply Chain Innovation and Application Pilot Program and corporate green innovation. Double machine learning is employed to account flexibly for nonlinear relationships between policy coverage, firm characteristics, and green innovation. Dual-policy coverage is positively and significantly associated with green invention patent applications, with a baseline coefficient of 0.1131. The result remains positive under alternative cross-fitting folds, machine learning algorithms, sample restrictions, and measures of green innovation. Channel analyses indicate that dual-policy coverage is associated with greater supply chain digitalization, lower supply chain risk, and higher innovation efficiency. The estimated association is stronger among firms with higher R&D intensity and weaker among firms facing greater environmental uncertainty. These findings provide firm-level evidence that logistics connectivity and supply chain organizational conditions are relevant to corporate green innovation and offer policy implications for sustainable industrial development.

title: Digital Transformation: Are Traditional Auditors' Competencies Sufficient for Remote ISO 14001 Audits?
summary: ABSTRACT This article explores how practitioners perceive the effects of digital transformation on ISO 14001 audits and on the competencies required to conduct them remotely. The study draws on 35 semi‐structured interviews with representatives of ISO‐14001‐certified organizations, external auditors, and consultants. While few studies have examined the digital transformation of ISO 14001 audit practices, this study shows how remote audits reshape verification practices, with greater reliance on documentary evidence and reduced opportunities for direct observation, while increasing the importance of auditors' technological, interpersonal, analytical, and investigative competencies. The analysis of these changes in verification practices and competency requirements contributes to the literature on the perceived rigor of audit evaluations and the credibility of ISO 14001 certification processes. The article contributes to research on the digitalization of assessment tools by showing how digital technologies transform the interpretation mechanisms used by auditors. The results call for adapting auditor training to preserve audit rigor.

title: Analysts’ use of toxic emissions data
summary: Purpose This study examines whether financial analysts function as information intermediaries by incorporating Toxics Release Inventory (TRI) data into their assessments of firms' environmental risks, as reflected in earnings forecasts and stock recommendations. It further investigates whether analysts' forecast and recommendation revisions influence subsequent corporate environmental performance, thereby providing evidence on the effectiveness of the Environmental Protection Agency's (EPA's) market-based regulatory approach. Design/methodology/approach Using a longitudinal sample of US publicly listed firms from 1997 to 2011, the study analyzes how financial analysts utilize TRI data in their decision-making processes. An event-study methodology is employed to examine how the EPA's annual public release of TRI data affects analysts' forecast accuracy and dispersion. The analysis also examines the economic implications of analysts' forecast and recommendation revisions for firms' future toxic emissions. Robustness tests are conducted using alternative environmental risk measures and industry-level analyses. Findings The results indicate that higher pollution propensity is associated with greater forecast errors and increased dispersion among analysts. Analysts respond to increases in pollution propensity by revising earnings forecasts and stock recommendations downward, and they revise them upward when pollution propensity declines. Importantly, these analyst responses are predictive of subsequent reductions in firms' toxic emissions, suggesting that analyst activity can exert real effects on corporate environmental behavior. Overall, the findings support the role of TRI disclosures in facilitating market-based discipline. Research limitations/implications The study is limited to US firms and TRI data up to 2011. Future research could investigate other forms of noncorporate disclosure and verifiable pollution data in global contexts to enhance the generalizability of the findings. Practical implications The study provides empirical support for the EPA's use of TRI disclosures as a mechanism to encourage environmental improvements through capital-market pressure. Policymakers and standard setters may further enhance the effectiveness of such disclosures by requiring more detailed and standardized environmental information in firms' management's discussion and analysis (MD&A), thereby enabling analysts to better identify and price environmental risks. Social implications By demonstrating that financial analysts incorporate TRI disclosures in ways that can shape firms' environmental behavior, the study underscores the social importance of public transparency in holding polluters accountable. Analysts' forecast revisions and stock recommendations can trigger market responses that incentivize greater corporate eco-efficiency, resulting in lower toxic emissions and improved environmental quality, thereby benefiting affected communities and reinforcing corporate environmental responsibility. Originality/value This study offers novel evidence that financial analysts incorporate nonfinancial, noncorporate TRI data into their analyses, highlighting their role as information intermediaries in an environmental reporting context. It demonstrates that analysts are able to parse the uncertainty inherent in TRI data and translate environmental risk into financial outcomes through earnings forecast and stock recommendation revisions. Additionally, the study documents tangible effects of analyst behavior on firms' pollution abatement efforts, contributing to the literature on environmental accounting, analyst behavior and market-based regulation, with important policy implications.

title: SPECIFIC FEATURES OF IMPROVING ACCOUNTING AND AUDITING SERVICES BASED ON INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS (THE EXPERIENCE OF UZBEKISTAN)
summary: This article analyzes the theoretical and practical aspects of improving accounting and auditing services based on international standards. In particular, it highlights the importance of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) and International Standards on Auditing (ISA) in economic development. It also examines the processes of adapting accounting and auditing activities to international standards in the Republic of Uzbekistan, the normative-legal documents adopted in this direction, and the ongoing reforms. The article analyzes the issues of training specialists with international accounting certificates in the country, increasing the transparency of financial reporting, and creating a favorable investment climate for investors. Furthermore, it outlines the problems arising during the implementation of international standards and ways to overcome them. The research results can serve to strengthen the integration of the country's economy into the international financial system by improving accounting and auditing services.

title: INTEGRATED MODEL OF ANALYSIS OF THE STATE OF CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY IN THE SYSTEM OF STRATEGIC MANAGEMENT OF HARMONIOUS DEVELOPMENT
summary: The article analyzes scientific works on the essence and state of corporate social responsibility (CSR) in the system of strategic management of harmonious development. The scientific novelty of the study lies in the formation of a comprehensive model of CSR analysis, which integrates the assessment of internal and external factors with the system of assessment directions. It is determined that the main directions of assessing the state of CSR are the market, working and environmental environment, as well as interaction with society. The practical value of the model lies in the possibility of its use by enterprises to improve the efficiency of CSR management and justify strategic decisions in the field of sustainable development. The proposed model allows ensuring the systematicity and consistency of the CSR assessment process and increases the level of objectivity of the analysis.

title: Banco general como actor del desarrollo sostenible en panamá: análisis de la integración de los objetivos de desarrollo sostenible y las finanzas sostenibles en sus reportes corporativos (2023-2025)
summary: Sustainability has become a strategic element for financial institutions due to growing demands for transparency, corporate responsibility and contributions to sustainable development. In this context, banks have assumed a relevant role in promoting responsible economic practices and aligning their strategies with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) of the United Nations 2030 Agenda. The objective of this study was to analyze Banco General's role as an actor of sustainable development in Panama through the integration of SDGs, sustainable finance and corporate social responsibility in its corporate reports during the period 2023–2025. A qualitative approach based on a case study design and documentary analysis of sustainability reports and institutional documents was employed. The findings reveal a progressive incorporation of international sustainability standards as well as actions related to financial inclusion, education, environmental management, corporate governance and sustainable finance. A significant alignment with several SDGs was identified, particularly those related to quality education, gender equality, decent work and economic growth, climate action and partnerships for the goals. It is concluded that Banco General has consolidated an institutional strategy oriented toward sustainable development, positioning itself as a benchmark within the Panamanian banking sector in sustainability and social value creation.

title: Surviving by Serving - the effects of rewarding usefulness
summary: How can a complex production network organize itself when no participant knows the global plan? We investigate a simple principle inspired by markets: producers persist longer when what they make is actually used. We call this principle “Surviving by Serving” (SbS). In a deliberately minimal model, agents transform existing products into new ones and thereby build fluctuating production and supply networks starting from a single inexhaustible resource. We compare SbS with systems in which survival is not rewarded and with a control in which the same reward events are redirected to randomly selected agents. Within the tested model and parameter ranges, linking survival to downstream use enables faster and broader exploration of product space while retaining a larger share of what has been discovered. It also gives rise to more persistent, repeatedly active production pathways and more pronounced cyclic structures. In a targeted-reward experiment, selectively supporting suppliers of designated products can increase delivery to the desired region, without specifying the supply chains needed to reach it. These results do not establish a universal law of self-organization. They show, however, that a minimal local feedback between usefulness and persistence can substantially reshape collective organization in this model and motivate tests of analogous mechanisms in richer economic and biological networks.

title: Human-Centric Talent di Era Digital
summary: Digital transformation and the development of artificial intelligence (AI) have reshaped how organizations manage talent, while creating a growing need to ensure that technology continues to support human roles, competencies, and well-being. This study aims to analyze the concept of human-centric talent in the context of the digital era, identify the key aspects that support its implementation, and examine the roles of AI, digital competencies, leadership, transparency, and human–technology collaboration in talent management. This study employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach by analyzing relevant scientific literature through the stages of identification, screening, evaluation, and thematic synthesis of findings. The results indicate that human-centric talent is not merely concerned with technology adoption but places people at the center of digital transformation through the development of digital competencies, adaptive leadership, transparent and fair AI implementation, and balanced collaboration between humans and technology. AI can improve the efficiency of various talent management functions but still requires human oversight, contextual judgment, and decision-making. The findings contribute conceptually by positioning human-centric talent as an integrative approach that connects technology, people, organizations, and governance. Practically, the study highlights the importance of competency development, human-centric leadership, responsible AI governance, and work design that preserves human involvement in the face of digital transformation.

title: A Hybrid Multi-Criteria Decision-Making Framework for Prioritizing Supply Chain Risks in Perishable Food Manufacturing
summary: Abstract Food-processing supply chains are severely threatened by interruptions in procurement, storage and transport due to the perishability of products and the strict delivery demands. Conventional risk models rank the importance of the factors, but do not differentiate the root causes from the downstream consequences. The study proposes a multi-method framework for assessing ten critical disruption factors with the use of expert judgments. AHP Establishes priority weights for strategic intervention. (F6) was perceived as the most important (RII) = 0.9857, but (F10) was the key root-cause driver (D - R = 1.574). AHP validated F10 as the highest priority for intervention (weight: 0.2189), followed by storage violations (F7) and demand spikes (F8). Highly visible disruptions are often symptoms not root causes. title: AMBIENT AIR POLLUTION IN GEORGIA: MAJOR SOURCES, AIR-QUALITY MONITORING, HEALTH IMPACTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT
summary: Ambient air pollution is a major environmental and public-health challenge, resulting from natural and anthropogenic sources. This review examines the principal characteristics of ambient air pollution in Georgia, focusing on anthropogenic emission sources, road transport, industrial activities, particulate matter, air-quality monitoring, health implications, and environmental governance. Particular attention is given to the growing contribution of road transport to urban air pollution, influenced by vehicle numbers, fleet age, maintenance conditions, fuel quality, and emission-control systems. Recent national developments indicate a substantial expansion of Georgia’s air-quality monitoring infrastructure. As of 2026, the national network comprises 18 monitoring stations, including 15 automatic and three mobile stations, which monitor major pollutants such as nitrogen oxides, ozone, sulfur dioxide, carbon monoxide, PM₁₀, and PM₂.₅. Nevertheless, fine particulate matter remains a significant concern, with reported urban concentrations exceeding the health-based guideline values established by the World Health Organization. Recent policy measures, including Euro 5 emission requirements and restrictions on the import of older vehicles, demonstrate progress toward stricter emission control. However, sustained improvements require an integrated air-quality management framework incorporating reliable monitoring, comprehensive emission inventories, source-apportionment studies, cleaner transport, effective enforcement, and evidence-based public-health policies. Aligning national standards and practices with internationally recognized guidelines remains essential for reducing population exposure and improving environmental quality.

title: Analysis of Management Strategy, Corporate Social Responsibility and High-Profile Firm Value In Indonesia
summary: Information regarding Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) can encourage investors to make decisions that enhance firm value. Efficient risk management in operational activities further increases firm value while minimizing potential operational failures. High-profile companies show greater interest in disclosing CSR activities due to high external sensitivity and media coverage. This study examines the moderating effects of risk management and media exposure on the impact of CSR on high-profile firm value in Indonesia from 2016 to 2018. Using a quantitative approach, secondary data from 69 observations were analyzed through Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). The empirical findings indicate that CSR has a significant positive effect on high-profile firm value. However, neither risk management nor media exposure moderates the relationship between CSR and firm value. These findings suggest that investors evaluate CSR implementation as a direct positive signal rather than focusing on risk disclosures or media coverage. Consequently, companies should prioritize genuine CSR practices to enhance corporate value, while regulators need to establish clearer standards for risk management disclosures.

title: Evaluation of PELITA Tembesi CSR Program Based on Community Satisfaction Measurement at PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk. - Offtake Stasiun Panaran
summary: The PELITA Tembesi corporate social responsibility (CSR) program, implemented by PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk. – Offtake Station Panaran, reflects the company’s social responsibility toward the community in Tembesi Village, Sagulung District, Batam City. Based on social mapping that identified low competitiveness, limited capacity, and restricted access to mentoring among SME actors and community groups, the program empowers the Creative Independent Women’s Group (KPKM)—comprising the Agro Hijau Women Farmers Group, Godhong Ku, and the Mutiara Bersinar Waste Bank—and the Lance Bersatu Cooperative on Lance Island. This study measures beneficiary satisfaction with program implementation using the Community Satisfaction Index (IKM) as an evaluation instrument. A descriptive quantitative survey was conducted with 31 direct beneficiaries, selected through accidental sampling, in mid-September 2025. The overall IKM was 3.67 (converted value 91.75), categorized as Very Good (quality grade A). Of the eight elements evaluated, Implementer Behavior scored highest (Very Good), whereas Program Recognition scored lowest (Good). Both subprograms performed very well, with scores of 3.66 for KPKM and 3.69 for the Lance Bersatu Cooperative.

title: International Comparison of the Singapore ETF Ecosystem
summary: This paper compares Singapore’s exchange-traded fund (ETF) ecosystem with those of the United States, Mainland China, Hong Kong, Europe, Taiwan and selected ASEAN markets. It treats the ETF market as an institutional ecosystem connecting issuers, authorized participants, market makers, index and data providers, trading and clearing infrastructure, regulation and investor channels. Comparative institutional analysis is organized around autonomy, efficiency, inclusiveness and sustainability: the location and accountability of critical capabilities, the quality and cost of market functioning, investor access, and continuity across market cycles. Dated market statistics and regulatory documents reveal different arrangements for coordinating these functions. For Singapore, recent growth in assets, trading and digital and retirement-channel participation coexists with concentrated exchange trading; these observations do not establish a market-wide liquidity deficit or its causes. The paper develops an ‘openly embedded’ model in which international participation complements locally anchored operational capabilities and supervisory interfaces. It proposes a staged roadmap covering core ETF liquidity, issuer and intermediary capacity, investor channels, regional connectivity and risk governance. Digital distribution, API-based information and supervisory technology connect these proposals to FinTech. The recommendations are policy options informed by comparison, not estimated causal effects. The contribution is a practical framework for translating international institutional experience into testable policy priorities for a small, open financial centre.

title: Developing Community Capabilities through Local Potential-Based Economic Empowerment: A Case Study of the KANERGI Program at PT Pertamina Patra Niaga Integrated Terminal Kendari
summary: Community empowerment through Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) should be assessed not only by the assistance and activities provided but also by communities’ ability to use these resources sustainably. This study analyzes community capability development through the KANERGI Program, implemented by PT Pertamina Patra Niaga Integrated Terminal Kendari, which builds on local fisheries potential in Mata Urban Village. Using a qualitative case study approach, data were collected through interviews with five administrators and members of the Permata Mitra Bersama group, observation, and documentation. The data were analyzed thematically, with the Capability Approach as the primary framework and Asset-Based Community Development as a supporting perspective. The findings show that program interventions contributed to the development of production, business management, marketing, and collective capabilities. These capabilities were manifested in independent production of fish floss and fish meatballs, financial record-keeping, and participation in marketing activities. The group’s involvement in business decisions, including setting selling prices, indicates the emergence of agency. However, the absence of a stable market shows that marketing capabilities still need strengthening. The study demonstrates that CSR-based empowerment can be understood as a process of converting resources into capabilities, functionings, and community agency.

title: Green transition and job losses
summary: Purpose This paper aims to highlight how green product trade has become a core growth driver of international trade, while the green transformation of enterprises driven by external green demand brings potential risks to the labor market. Design/methodology/approach Based on the construction idea of the Bartik instrumental variable, this paper uses the import data of green products at the HS 6-digit level from 207 countries and regions around the world from 2007 to 2016, matches the export information of Chinese enterprises, measures the changes in the demand share of green products in destination countries, and identifies the green transition induced by exogenous demand shocks. Findings The study finds that a one-unit increase in green transition leads to approximately 13.37% job losses, but it simultaneously optimizes the labor skill structure. The share of low-skilled labor decreases by about 4.58% points, while the share of high-skilled labor increases by roughly 0.97% points. This conclusion remains robust after a series of robustness tests. Mechanism tests indicate that enterprises achieve employment optimization through scale effects in energy input, green innovation effects, and product structure adjustment effects. The results of extended analysis indicate that employment in labor-intensive enterprises, enterprises with high artificial intelligence adoption, enterprises in highly competitive industries, and those with high market exposure is more significantly affected by the green transition. The findings of this paper provide managerial implications for firms' employment decisions in response to green transition. Originality/value The marginal contributions of this paper can be summarized as follows: First, due to the inconsistent definitions of green products and the lack of a unified method for measuring exports, this paper comprehensively collates green product list data with certain international consensus, providing new data references for research on green product exports. Second, this paper measures green transition through changes in exogenous demand share, avoiding the limitations of traditional models that rely on endogenous variables such as technological progress, thereby more directly identifying the causal effect of demand-side-driven green transition. Starting from the micro enterprise level, this paper uses the actual import data of HS6-digit green products from 207 export destinations of China during 2007–2016, matching the enterprise export product market structure information and enterprise export production information in the China Customs Database. Based on this, the paper constructs a Bartik instrumental variable to measure changes in green product demand shocks from export destination countries, and empirically studies the relationship between green transition and employment. Third, this paper broadens the perspective of existing research by examining the impact and mechanism of green transition from two aspects: total labor scale and labor skill structure, supplementing the research dimension of the impact of exports on employment.

title: ESG Risk and Financial Performance in Apparel Supply Chains: Evidence from NYSE and NASDAQ Listed US Companies (2021–2024)
summary: Abstract This study investigates the relationship between Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) risk and the financial performance of apparel companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and the NASDAQ. The apparel industry is highly vulnerable to sustainability-related risks in its supply chains, and existing evidence on the relationship between ESG and financial performance remains fragmented and inconsistent across industries and regions. Therefore, this study examines whether the relationship between ESG and financial performance has existed in one specific market, the apparel industry, after the COVID-19 pandemic. Using a panel of 30 US-listed apparel companies observed from 2021 to 2024 (120 firm-year observations), pooled Ordinary Least Squares regression with standard errors clustered by firm was used to test the relationship between Sustainalytics' ESG Risk Score and two measures of financial performance: Return on Assets (ROA) and Net Profit Margin (NPM). The results reveal a statistically significant negative relationship between the ESG Risk Score and ROA and with NPM, respectively, suggesting that companies with a lower ESG Risk Score (better ESG Risk Management) have better financial performance. This relationship strengthens when the analysis is limited to the years 2022–2024, excluding the atypical post-pandemic recovery year of 2021, and is significant in most robustness checks, including outlier and multicollinearity tests. The results provide context-specific evidence for a body of literature with mixed findings across industries and regions, and could be relevant to apparel company managers and investors assessing the financial relevance of ESG risk management.

title: When Innovation Becomes Community-Owned: How the Diffusion of Food Waste-Based Alternative Feed Innovation Occurs Among Fish Farmers in Sungai Gerong Village
summary: High feed costs remain a major challenge in fish farming because they raise production expenses and limit farmers’ profit margins. Through its Belida Musi Lestari Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Program, PT Pertamina Patra Niaga RU III Plaju introduced food waste-based alternative feed as a substitute feed ingredient. This study analyzes the diffusion of this innovation among fish farmer groups in Sungai Gerong Village using Rogers’ innovation-decision process framework. A qualitative case study was conducted through interviews, observations, documentation, and group discussions. The findings show that diffusion proceeded through five stages: knowledge, persuasion, decision, implementation, and confirmation. Each stage was shaped by interactions among change agents, opinion leaders, and group members. The CSR team, academics, and fisheries extension officers introduced the innovation, while the local hero encouraged adoption through experimentation and the development of feed formulations suited to local conditions. The study also identified reinvention, whereby feed formulations and feeding practices were modified based on farmers’ experiences and the availability of local raw materials. Sustained adoption depended on continuous assistance and a stable supply of food waste. These findings indicate that successful community-based innovation diffusion requires synergy among appropriate technology, local actors, and a supportive innovation ecosystem.

title: Compliance in digital innovation: Managing digital transformation at Treasury Bank
summary: Digital transformation has become a strategic priority for banks seeking to improve operational efficiency, strengthen controls, and remain competitive. In highly regulated environments, however, technology projects cannot be evaluated on operational merit alone; they must also satisfy regulatory, security, audit, and governance requirements. This teaching case examines the implementation of an outsourced Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) high-value payment processing system at ‘Treasury Bank’, a large commercial bank, and traces how compliance shaped decision-making across the entire project lifecycle. What began as a seemingly straightforward automation of a manual, email- and paper-based treasury process evolved into a broader organisational transformation involving Compliance, Risk Management, Information Security, System Audit, Legal, and Data Governance functions. The case follows five implementation phases – project assessment, vendor assessment and business approval, system development, testing and validation, and go-live – showing how governance reviews influenced vendor selection, security assessments, audit requirements, and final approvals. Drawing on interviews with business and IT stakeholders directly involved in the project, the case highlights both the benefits of embedding compliance throughout the transformation, including stronger controls, greater transparency, improved auditability, and higher system quality, and the challenges this approach created, such as additional reviews, increased coordination, and extended timelines. It concludes with the strategic dilemma facing senior management: how to maintain robust compliance and governance while keeping digital transformation responsive and timely. The case suits undergraduate and postgraduate courses in Information Systems, IT Governance, Digital Transformation, and related fields.

title: ESG Governance and Sustainable Islamic Finance in Malaysia, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia and UAE
summary: Growing dissatisfaction with symbolic ESG compliance has exposed a governance gap in sustainable finance: ethical commitments are expanding faster than mechanisms capable of converting them into measurable environmental and social outcomes. This study examines how ESG governance can function as an institutional bridge between sustainable finance and Islamic finance, with relevance to Malaysia, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia and the UAE. Following PRISMA 2020, 29 records identified through Web of Science, Scopus and Emerald Insight were screened, yielding 15 peer-reviewed studies published between 2024 and 2026 for qualitative thematic analysis. Five interconnected themes emerged: normative convergence between ESG and Islamic ethical finance; governance and institutional accountability; Islamic social finance and inclusive sustainability; disclosure, transparency and legitimacy; and digital transformation and impact measurement. The findings show that ethical compatibility alone does not generate credible sustainability outcomes. Strong internal governance, including sustainability committees, Shariah supervisory boards, ESG oversight and integrated reporting, emerges as the critical mechanism separating substantive sustainability from symbolic compliance. Islamic social finance remains notably under-integrated into formal ESG architectures, while existing disclosures are frequently governance-heavy but metric-light. Digital technologies can strengthen traceability and impact measurement, but only when embedded within robust governance systems. This study develops an integrated ESG–Islamic governance framework that translates Maqasid al-Shariah principles into measurable accountability, impact verification and scalable green-development mechanisms. It reframes ESG from a reporting regime into governance infrastructure for ethical, inclusive and resilient finance, offering actionable implications for regulators, financial institutions and sustainability standard-setters.

title: Industry 4.0, Quality and Industry 4.0. Implementation in Slovakia: A Longitudinal Analysis Based on the Industry 4UM Survey (2017–2025)
summary: Industry 4.0 has become a key driver of industrial digital transformation, enabling enterprises to improve productivity, flexibility, and competitiveness through the integration of advanced digital technologies. Although the strategic importance of Industry 4.0 is widely recognized, the pace and maturity of its implementation vary considerably across enterprises and regions. This study presents a longitudinal evaluation of Industry 4.0 adoption in the Slovak Republic based on annual Industry4UM survey data collected between 2017 and 2025. The analysis focuses on three indicators: the size distribution of participating enterprises, the implementation phase of Industry 4.0, and the perceived importance of Industry 4.0 for future business development. The results indicate that the survey maintained participation from enterprises of different sizes throughout the observation period, providing a broad representation of the Slovak industrial environment. The implementation analysis revealed a gradual increase in the proportion of enterprises reaching the adaptation phase, accompanied by a substantial decline in the number of organizations that had not yet initiated Industry 4.0 activities. At the same time, respondents consistently expressed a highly positive perception of Industry 4.0, while negative attitudes remained negligible. A comparison of enterprise perception and implementation demonstrates that awareness of Industry 4.0 has advanced more rapidly than practical adoption, indicating that the principal challenge is no longer recognizing the importance of digital transformation but facilitating its effective implementation. The findings provide a comprehensive overview of the evolution of Industry 4.0 adoption in Slovak industry and offer insights that may support policymakers, researchers, and industrial practitioners in designing future digital transformation strategies. In this article, we also examine the State of Israel’s approach to Industry 4.0 from several perspectives. We focus on how both the Israeli industrial sector and government agencies support and implement Industry 4.0. Israeli government agencies, businesses, and institutions also focus on social and economic issues and on structural changes in the labour market related to Industry 4.0.

title: Beyond compliance: Community development committees and the transformation of resource governance in Tanzania
summary: Resource-rich countries worldwide often face persistent imbalances in the redistribution of resource wealth. Although mineral extraction generates substantial revenues, these funds are typically centrally managed and redistributed, leaving host communities, who bear the social and environmental burdens of extraction, impoverished and marginalized. In Tanzania, despite provisions allowing Local Government Authorities to levy a 0.3% service charge on mining revenues and receive Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) contributions intended to support local development, means of engaging host communities remain a challenge. Community Development Agreements (CDAs) have been identified as potential instruments to safeguard the interests of host communities. However, despite their widespread promotion, a critical gap remains in understanding how communities can effectively engage in, negotiate, and implement CDAs, particularly in contexts marked by power asymmetries. Communities are often poor, with limited knowledge of mining and the broader extractive industry, and with no access to decision-making power. This study addresses the gap by examining Community Development Committees (CDCs) as an inclusive, participatory institutional mechanism through which communities can effectively articulate their development priorities. Using semi‑structured interviews with 36 key informants across the mining value chain, including central government officials, mining representatives, and local communities, the study finds the CDC model as an effective approach for strengthening community voice, enhancing transparency, improving negotiations, and monitoring project implementations. Although grounded in Tanzania’s mining sector, the study offers insights relevant to other resource dependent economies seeking to foster more equitable social contracts.

title: The Effect of Profit Growth, Capital Structure, and Independent Commissioners on Company Value at PT. Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa Tbk Period 2015 - 2025
summary: The decline in the company value of PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa Tbk during the 2015-2025 period indicates the need to examine the factors that influence company value. This study aims to analyze the effect of profit growth, capital structure, and independent commissioners on company value. This study uses a quantitative method with a causal associative approach and secondary data in the form of annual reports, sustainability reports, and stock price data of PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa Tbk for the 2015-2025 period. The population and sample of the study are financial data and corporate governance during the observation period selected using purposive sampling. Data collection was carried out through documentation and analyzed using SPSS 27 through descriptive statistics, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression, coefficient of determination, F tests, and t tests. The results of the study indicate that profit growth does not have a significant effect on company value, capital structure has a significant effect with a negative direction, while independent commissioners have no significant effect. In conclusion, capital structure is a factor that significantly influences company value in this study.

title: RISK-ORIENTED STRATEGIC MANAGEMENT MECHANISMS OF OIL AND GAS COMPANIES IN THE CONTEXT OF DIGITAL ECOSYSTEMS DEVELOPMENT
summary: The article examines the improvement of risk-oriented strategic management mechanisms of oil and gas companies against the backdrop of the rapid development of digital ecosystems. The transition from traditional vertical integration to a digital platform model has fundamentally altered the nature of risks in the energy sector. The study evaluates the role of Big Data, intelligent analytics, and agile management methodologies in minimizing risks. To form a modern management system, a synthesis of strategic planning and forecasting of digital risks is proposed. Consequently, a flexible and decentralized risk management model that ensures the sustainable development of industrial enterprises is substantiated. The digital transformation environment creates new technological threats in the oil and gas industry, such as cybersecurity issues and data dependency. For this reason, traditional reactive management methods lose their effectiveness, making proactive approaches a necessity. In the course of the research, the application of scenario analysis and predictive analytics tools comes to the forefront. The proposed innovative mechanism increases the speed of decision-making by companies, ensures the flexibility of internal structures, and strengthens corporate resilience. This approach enhances the energy sector's stability against global macroeconomic shocks and market volatility, fundamentally securing the competitiveness of the national industry in the digital era. Keywords: digital ecosystem, oil and gas sector, risk-oriented management, strategic mechanisms, digital transformation.

title: From experiential to computational trust: how data-driven decision-making enhances ESG performance in emerging market supply chains
summary: Emerging-market supply chains face growing ESG pressure, yet governance based on experiential trust often falls short in complex sustainability decisions. Drawing on the DECAS framework, this study examines how data-driven decision-making reshapes relational learning from experiential trust to computational trust and, in turn, improves ESG performance. Using panel data on Chinese A-share listed supply chain firms from 2015 to 2024, we find that DDDM significantly improves ESG performance. This effect works through two reinforcing channels: higher investment efficiency and stronger collaborative innovation. We also find that internationalisation strengthens the role of collaborative innovation. By introducing computational trust into the analysis, this study offers a clearer explanation of how data and analytics support sustainable supply chain governance. It extends the application of DECAS in ESG research and provides evidence that firms can improve sustainable performance by combining better resource allocation with stronger interorganizational innovation.

title: Accounting Practices and Quality of Financial Reporting in Public Secondary Schools in Nairobi City County, Kenya
summary: Methodology: For research design, the study utilized descriptive research and it encompassed both quantitative and qualitative analysis. The research utilized structured questionnaires to gather data and were distributed to 210 respondents who formed the sample drawn from total target populace. Data was analyzed using inferential statistics to find patterns and create predictive models, descriptive statistics provided an overview of the data. Findings: Findings showed that digital accounting practices, bookkeeping, internal controls and budgeting together account for 67.0% of the variation in reporting quality. The study also established that internal controls (β=0.261; p=0.000), budgeting practices (β=0.250; p=0.000), bookkeeping practices (β=0.277; p=0.000) and digital accounting practices (β=0.238; p=0.000) had significant effect on quality of financial reporting. Unique Contribution to Theory, Policy and Practice: The study contributes to theory as it deduced that robust accounting procedures are necessary for transparency, accuracy and accountability, both individually and collectively within public secondary schools. The study recommends that Principals need to take charge and set up strong internal controls of schools want to prevent conflicts of interest and to hold people accountable. This is made possible when they make clear who handles money. It is also recommended that County education and treasury officers should check in often and offer hands-on training in financial management. When schools tighten up these controls, it gets a lot harder for anyone to misuse funds.

title: Reshaping global value chains in the digital era: a systematic review from a firm-based perspective
summary: Purpose This study aims to systematically examine how digitalization reshapes global value chains (GVCs) from a firm-centric perspective. It seeks to integrate theoretical insights and identify the antecedents, transformation processes, outcomes and moderating factors of digital GVC restructuring. Design/methodology/approach A systematic review of 39 empirical articles (2014–2024) integrates the ownership–location–internalization (OLI) paradigm and stakeholder theory to construct a multidimensional framework that captures firms’ strategic responses to digital transformation. Findings The review reveals that digitalization reshapes GVCs through reconfiguration of ownership advantages (e.g. digital capabilities), location strategies (e.g. digital infrastructure and regulatory environments) and internalization mechanisms (e.g. platform integration and blockchain). Outcomes include enhanced firm performance and governance innovation, as well as social and environmental challenges. These effects are moderated by national institutions, industry characteristics and firm-specific capabilities, resulting in uneven digital dividends and risks. Originality/value This study contributes to international business research by (1) linking micro-level firm strategies with macro-level GVC changes, (2) offering an integrated theoretical lens combining OLI and stakeholder perspectives and (3) highlighting underexplored issues such as power asymmetries and ecological trade-offs in digitalized GVCs. It provides a clear agenda for future research and practical recommendations for firms navigating digital transformation in global contexts.

title: Digital transformation of international organisations: navigating between utopia and shipwreck
summary: Introduction Digital transformation promises greater efficiency and cooperation among international organisations but also risks fragmentation, weakened sovereignty, and exclusion. This paper uses regime complex theory to examine how international organisations navigate these competing pressures. Methods A structured, focused comparative case study approach is applied to selected regional frameworks and international organisation initiatives, including ASEAN’s Digital Economy Framework Agreement, APEC’s Cross-Border Privacy Rules, UNDP’s Digital Strategy, and WFP’s Building Blocks. Documentary analysis examines institutional overlap, authority relationships, and actor strategies. Results The analysis identifies six interconnected governance dimensions: institutional foundations, sovereignty–interoperability tensions, digital public goods, algorithmic diplomacy, cybersecurity, and implementation pathways. Across cases, effective digital transformation depends on legitimacy, accountability, and stakeholder trust. Flexible coordination helps manage sovereignty–interoperability tensions, while AI bias and unequal cybersecurity capacities require inclusive oversight and collective responses. Discussion Digital transformation in international organisations is fundamentally a political rather than merely technical challenge. The paper proposes a minimum-variable governance framework and a four-phase implementation roadmap to balance innovation with institutional integrity. These proposals emphasise adaptive governance, equity, and sustained institution-building as foundations for sustainable digital transformation.

title: Ethical Risks of Generative Large Language Models and Corporate Social Responsibility Performance: Evidence from China
summary: The ethical risks associated with generative large language models (GLLMs) raise concerns about their implications for corporate social responsibility (CSR). Drawing on firm-year observations for Chinese A-share companies over 2015–2024, we investigate how GLLM-related ethical risk relates to CSR performance. A firm-level disclosure-based measure of GLLM-related ethical risk signals is constructed from annual-report text and analyzed using two-way fixed-effect models. The results show a negative and statistically significant association, with higher ethical risk corresponding to lower subsequent CSR performance. This association persists across robustness checks and instrumental variable analyses. Firm-clustered bootstrap analyses reveal significant negative indirect associations through reputational pressure and financing constraints, supporting the proposed mediating pathways. Managerial compliance attention strengthens the negative association between ethical risk and CSR performance. These findings extend research on the antecedents of CSR by identifying the ethical risks of emerging technologies as a relevant organizational concern. They also highlight the importance of integrating ethical AI governance with CSR planning to support responsible technology adoption and sustained corporate sustainability commitments.

title: Dispossession by digital consolidation: Early notes on the crisis of the media and entertainment sector in Mumbai, India
summary: The ongoing wave of consolidation and digital transformation in the Mumbai-based media and entertainment sector, the heart of Hindi cultural production, has brought about an unparalleled alignment of interests between media and big tech. As a result, the sector has begun to assume a bifurcated structure, comprising a limited set of major incumbents and a substantial population of smaller entities, with a gradual erosion of the culturally significant middle segment. Creative work has become more casualised and compensation lower even as the sector’s overall revenues expand. Drawing on interactions with creative workers in the sector, this article seeks to map the broad contours of the digital disruption – market concentration, big tech governance of the creative sector, the resultant crisis of production as reflected in the emerging micro-drama space, and creative workers’ articulation of the issues – and foreground the social and cultural costs of rapid and largely unchecked consolidation and digitisation.

title: Economic impacts of subsea cable deployment
summary: This paper provides a comprehensive empirical analysis of the economic impact of submarine cable (SMC) infrastructure, which is critical for global digital connectivity and carries almost all intercontinental data traffic. Despite their fundamental role in the digital economy, robust evidence on the economic returns of SMC investments is very scarce. To address this, we use a panel dataset of developed countries and causal identification strategies, such as two-way fixed effects models and instrumental variables exploiting exogenous variation from factors like a country's coastline length and legacy market competition. In our empirical analysis we first describe how international bandwidth (IBW) can be used as a proxy for SMC capacity and examine how it affects domestic broadband quality levels. We then quantify the impact on broadband demand, finding distinct yet robust demand elasticities for mobile and fixed services. We find that a 1% increase in IBW drives an increase in mobile broadband adoption between 0.049% and 0.081%, while the increase for fixed broadband adoption ranges between 0.056% and 0.061%. Finally, we translate these estimates into a simple cost-benefit framework using an illustrative transatlantic cable project connecting Ireland and the United States. This analysis shows that the substantial GDP spillovers overwhelmingly exceed the total private deployment costs. Our findings affirm that SMC deployments generate significant positive externalities and high social returns. While it has been argued in the previous literature that these effects are critical to developing nations lacking infrastructure, our findings indicate this effect is also applicable to advanced economies. Consequently, we argue that policymakers in coastal nations, regardless of their level of development, have a strong economic incentive to facilitate private investment by reducing regulatory barriers and transaction costs associated with, for example, cable permits and landing stations.

title: Institutional Ownership and Corporate Exposure to Equal Employment Opportunity Lawsuits
summary: ABSTRACT Research Question/Issue This study investigates whether and how institutional ownership is associated with firms' exposure to equal employment opportunity (EEO) lawsuits under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964. These lawsuits capture an underexplored form of downside ESG risk arising from firms' treatment of employees, who constitute a key corporate stakeholder group. Research Findings/Insights Using a dataset of 22,501 EEO lawsuits filed in US federal courts from 2001 to 2020, this study finds that firms with higher institutional blockholdings experience significantly fewer EEO lawsuits. This relationship persists across active, passive, long‐term, and transient investors and remains robust to an instrumental variable analysis exploiting Russell 3000 Index inclusion, change analyses, industry adjustments, and numerous robustness tests. Post‐lawsuit responses reveal three mechanisms: The largest investors withdraw capital (exit); transient investors increase voting engagement (voice); and forced CEO turnover increases, particularly in high‐blockholding firms (discipline). Institutional investors' role is amplified in low‐skilled labor environments and complemented by independent board monitoring. Theoretical/Academic Implications This study documents the role of institutional investors in mitigating the risk of workplace discrimination litigation, advancing the literature on institutional monitoring, ESG, employee welfare, and corporate governance. EEO lawsuits provide an objective, non‐self‐reported measure of a specific downside ESG risk. This study further shows how heterogeneous investors deploy different mechanisms to improve EEO outcomes. Practitioner/Policy Implications Workplace discrimination poses a threat to employee well‐being and firm reputation. Uncovering institutional investors' role in safeguarding employees' civil right to EEO provides useful insights for policymakers, boards, and investors.

title: Competencies for Sustainable Development in Entrepreneurship: A Bibliometric Analysis
summary: ABSTRACT Sustainability has become one of society's main concerns and, with it, the development of the competencies necessary to achieve and contribute to sustainable development. In this sense, the entrepreneur as an agent of change toward a sustainable world is fundamental. This paper contributes to the knowledge on competencies for sustainable development in entrepreneurship by conducting a bibliometric analysis. The results show significant growth in the literature, especially since 2017, and reveal five thematic clusters linked to individual and strategic capabilities for sustainable performance, sustainable entrepreneurship ecosystems, education for sustainable entrepreneurship, social entrepreneurship and digital transformation in emerging economies, and women's empowerment and well‐being. This study demonstrates that competencies for sustainable development are a key element enabling entrepreneurs to transform social and environmental challenges into opportunities for innovation, value creation, and transition toward more sustainable business models. Furthermore, future research lines are suggested to further explore entrepreneurship based on sustainable competencies.

title: Female CEOs and board gender diversity: catalysts or constraints?
summary: Purpose The objective of this study is to examine the effects of CEO gender on female board appointments. Given the substantial influence of CEOs on director selection and board composition, this study concentrates on CEO attributes. Design/methodology/approach Using a sample of 3,001 US listed firms over the period from 1999 to 2014, this study examines the relationship between CEO gender and the appointment of female directors on corporate boards. Findings The results show that firms led by female CEOs appoint more female directors on their boards, consistent with the socio-psychological perspective of similarity-attraction rather than the signaling theory. Furthermore, the positive effect of female CEOs on female director appointments is stronger when the CEO's tenure is shorter and when the newly appointed female CEO succeeds a male CEO. Originality/value This study contributes to the corporate governance literature by examining the antecedents of board composition at the organizational level. As such, it provides empirical support that a CEO's needs and desires can be demand-side factors influencing the phenomenon of female director selection. This study also contributes to female leadership literature by providing a method that female CEOs can use (i.e. appointing more female directors) to overcome the difficulties they face.

title: Digital communication in Peru’s public museums: a mixed analysis
summary: Digital transformation has changed the way museums interact with their audiences, creating new opportunities to expand access to cultural heritage. The objective of this study was to analyze the digital communication strategies used by public museums in Peru using a mixed methodological approach. In the quantitative phase, 27 digital communication indicators were evaluated in the 56 public museums recognized by the Ministry of Culture, while in the qualitative phase, semi-structured interviews were conducted with five key informants from the museum sector. The results show a widespread presence of digital platforms, but with limited levels of updating, interaction, and adoption of immersive technologies. Institutional barriers related to budgetary constraints, bureaucratic processes, and technological infrastructure gaps were also identified. The study concludes that digital communication in Peruvian museums is in a transition phase toward hybrid models that integrate face-to-face and virtual experiences to strengthen cultural participation.

title: Sustainable project management as a lever for competitiveness: a case study in the portuguese furniture industry
summary: The growing environmental, social, and regulatory pressures have made sustainability a central concern for industrial organisations, particularly in sectors with significant resource consumption, such as the furniture industry. In this context, the integration of ESG (Environmental, Social and Governance) criteria into project management has emerged as a critical factor for improving organisational performance and long-term competitiveness. This research explores how sustainable project management can act as a strategic lever within the Portuguese furniture industry. A mixed-method approach was adopted, combining a bibliometric analysis of recent scientific literature with an in-depth case study of AM Furniture Group. The bibliometric analysis highlights a clear increase in academic interest in sustainability within project management, with a strong emphasis on environmental and governance dimensions, while the social dimension remains comparatively less explored. Complementing this, the case study provides practical insights into how ESG principles are embedded in real organisational contexts. The findings show that sustainability is being operationalised through concrete practices, including the use of certified materials, investment in energy efficiency, adoption of eco-design principles, and the implementation of hybrid project management methodologies that balance structure with flexibility. These practices not only reduce environmental impact but also enhance innovation capacity, operational efficiency, and responsiveness to market demands. Overall, the study demonstrates that sustainable project management should not be viewed merely as a compliance requirement but as a strategic approach that supports value creation, strengthens competitive positioning, and aligns business objectives with broader environmental and social responsibilities. This perspective is particularly relevant for traditional industries undergoing transformation, such as the Portuguese furniture sector, where sustainability can play a decisive role in future growth and differentiation.

title: How AI-Driven Intelligent Financial Systems Improve Cost Control Efficiency in SMEs
summary: This study evaluated how AI intelligent financial systems affect cost control efficiency in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). It was conducted because existing literature focuses heavily on macro-level adoption, ignoring micro-level workflows and leaving managers unsure about actual investment returns. A theoretical model based on decision delay, human-machine synergy, and investment boundaries was tested using survey data from 218 SMEs in the Yangtze River Delta. Results showed that efficiency depends on reducing delays, accurate cost prediction, and rational technical input, with prediction accuracy having the strongest impact. Data also proved an inverted U-shaped boundary for AI investment, where both under-investment and over-investment decrease net income. This means digital transformation value is jointly shaped by technology, organizational capability, and resource constraints, proving SMEs must identify optimal investment scales rather than just buying advanced systems.

title: Pengaruh Accrual Earnings Management dan ESG disclosure terhadap Capital Structure: Studi pada Perusahaan Non-keuangan yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia
summary: Studi ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh accrual earnings management dan ESG disclosure terhadap capital structure di perusahaan non-keuangan yang terdaftar di BEI periode 2020-2024. Studi ini mempergunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan data sekunder dan teknik purposive sampling. Analisis dilaksanakan mempergunakan regresi linear. Temuan studi ini memperlihatkan bahwasanya accrual earnings management dan ESG disclosure dapat memengaruhi signifikan negatif terhadap capital structure. Temuan tersebut memperlihatkan bahwasanya perusahaan yang menerapkan manajemen laba serta mempunyai tingkat pengungkapan ESG lebih tinggi cenderung mempunyai tingkat leverage lebih rendah. Studi ini memberikan bukti empiris yang dapat memperkaya literatur bidang akuntansi dan keuangan, sekaligus menjadi bahan pertimbangan bagi perusahaan menetapkan kebijakan pendanaan optimal. Implikasi penelitian menunjukkan pentingnya transparansi informasi dan kualitas pelaporan keuangan dalam mendukung Keputusan pendanaan. Hasil penelitian ini juga dapat menjadi referensi bagi investor, manajemen, dan pemangku kepentingan dalam mengevaluasi risiko keuangan, tata kelola, serta strategi perusahaan secara lebih komprehensif dan berkelanjutan untuk menghadapi perubahan lingkungan bisnis global.

title: Impact of artificial intelligence on project planning, scheduling, and control
summary: Abstract The growing complexity of engineering and construction projects has revealed the weaknesses of conventional project planning, scheduling, and control approaches. Traditional tools often employ fixed assumptions, deterministic models, and past averages, which are inadequate for dealing with uncertainty, dynamic environments, and large-scale data. Artificial intelligence has become a disruptive technology that can be used to improve decision-making, prediction, and automation in project management processes. This paper examines the application of artificial intelligence in project planning, scheduling, and control within the engineering and construction sector. The paper summarises the application of artificial intelligence methods, including machine learning, optimization algorithms, and predictive analytics, in enhancing project performance using a methodical review of the recent scholarly literature and industry practise. The results show that artificial intelligence promotes the planning accuracy, flexibility of scheduling, and real-time project control to a great extent, as it allows data-driven insights and flexible responses. Issues of data quality, company preparedness, and ethical issues are major obstacles to implementation. The research paper adds to the project management literature because it develops the application of artificial intelligence in the three fundamental project management functions and provides practical advice to practitioners interested in introducing intelligent project management systems. Keywords Artificial intelligence, project planning, project scheduling, project control, construction management, digital transformation

title: Research on the Current Status and Influencing Factors of the Digital Transformation of Small and Micro Enterprises in Shanghai
summary: Enterprise digitalization has become a key measure for enhancing corporate competitiveness and promoting the development of the digital economy. Drawing on questionnaire survey data, this paper quantitatively evaluates the degree of digital transformation of small and micro enterprises in Shanghai along multiple dimensions, including industry, development stage, and position in the industrial chain. On this basis, it constructs an evaluation index system and applies the fuzzy analytic hierarchy process to identify the influencing factors. The results show that, at the criterion level, the participant factor has the greatest impact on the digital transformation of small and micro enterprises in Shanghai, followed in descending order by organizational, task, and technological factors; at the indicator level, the factors with the greatest impact are customer satisfaction, strategic planning for digital transformation, market incentives, and information security and risk prevention and control. Accordingly, this paper puts forward policy recommendations on improving customer satisfaction, refining the market incentive mechanism, attaching greater importance to information security and risk prevention and control, and establishing a multi-dimensional collaborative support system, with a view to advancing the digital transformation of small and micro enterprises in Shanghai.

title: A Qualitative Study on Food Waste Management in Food and Beverage Businesses: The Case of Beykoz District
summary: Sustainability and food waste management have become central to the global agenda in response to the rapid depletion of natural resources and escalating environmental challenges. The food and beverage sector, in particular, constitutes a critical component of these discussions due to its intensive consumption of energy and water, as well as the substantial amounts of waste generated throughout production and consumption processes. The aim of this study is to conduct an in-depth qualitative analysis of food waste management practices within food and beverage establishments, alongside an examination of their potential for digital transformation. In this context, the study explores businesses’ levels of awareness regarding waste management, their digital infrastructures, their engagement with smart technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT), and their perceptions of sustainability. The research population comprises restaurants and cafés operating in the Beykoz district of Istanbul Data were collected through semi-structured, face-to-face interviews conducted with the managers or owners of eight establishments selected via purposive sampling. The data obtained were analyzed using qualitative content analysis. The principal findings indicate that waste management practices within these establishments are generally confined to compliance with legal requirements and the implementation of ad hoc practical measures. Systematic approaches such as source separation of waste and technology-supported inventory management remain limited. Furthermore, the findings reveal a low level of awareness concerning digitalisation and IoT technologies, while cost pressures and operational intensity emerge as significant barriers to the adoption of sustainable practices. These results suggest that local authorities should develop incentive-based policies, organise targeted training programmes, and provide support for digital infrastructure in order to facilitate the transition towards sustainable and smart restaurant models within the sector.

title: Fiscal–ESG governance coherence: Examining regulatory fragmentation in Indonesia’s sustainability governance
summary: As sustainability increasingly shapes governance and accountability agendas, the relationship between fiscal policy and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) frameworks warrants closer examination. This study examines how taxation and sustainability are framed within Indonesia's fiscal and sustainable finance regulatory frameworks, focusing on the explicit linkage between fiscal contribution and ESG accountability. It applies qualitative document analysis and abductive thematic analysis to Indonesia's Tax Harmonization Law, the Sustainable Finance Roadmap Phase II, and OJK Regulation No. 51 of 2017. Documents were manually coded and analyzed across three dimensions: institutional mandate, policy instrument, and evaluative alignment. The findings show that taxation is framed primarily around fiscal resilience and development financing, whereas ESG governance emphasizes risk management and disclosure-based accountability. Although both domains address aspects of sustainability, the regulatory instruments examined establish limited explicit connections between taxation and ESG governance, particularly regarding the inclusion of fiscal contribution in ESG evaluative mechanisms. This indicates a gap in regulatory alignment, rather than demonstrating complete separation in practice. The study introduces Fiscal–ESG Governance Coherence as an analytical lens for assessing fiscal-sustainability alignment across institutional mandate, policy instrument, and evaluative mechanism at the regulatory design level. The findings highlight opportunities to strengthen the relationship between fiscal accountability and sustainability governance.

title: Green Accounting, Eco-Innovation, and ESG Performance: Dynamic Effects, Mediation, and Threshold Evidence
summary: This study examines the dynamic and non-linear relationships among green accounting (GA), eco-innovation (EI), and ESG performance. Drawing on Legitimacy Theory and the Natural Resource-Based View, the study investigates whether GA and EI independently contribute to ESG performance, whether EI mediates the GA–ESG relationship, and whether a critical level of EI changes the contribution of GA to ESG performance. The analysis uses an unbalanced panel of 500 multinational corporations observed between 2015 and 2025. Two-Step System Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) is employed to address dynamic persistence and potential endogeneity, while Panel Threshold Analysis is used to identify regime-dependent effects. The findings indicate that both GA and EI are positively associated with ESG performance, with EI also functioning as an important transmission mechanism between GA and ESG. Furthermore, the positive contribution of GA becomes substantially stronger when firms exceed a critical eco-innovation threshold of approximately ten green patents per year. ESG performance also demonstrates significant intertemporal persistence. These findings highlight the importance of integrating environmental accounting with substantive innovation capabilities rather than treating sustainability disclosure as an isolated practice. The study offers theoretical implications for sustainability and resource-based perspectives and practical implications for corporate strategy and green policy design.

title: Bio-Integrated Quantum Diamond Sensors: Room-Temperature Sub-Cellular Magnetometry and Somatic Cryptographic Interlocks
summary: Emerging brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), electroceutical implants, and continuous physiological monitoring systems rely on invasive metallic microelectrodes or classical bio-potential sensors. These technologies suffer from three fatal limitations: (1) biological foreign-body responses, glial scarring, and neuro-inflammatory degradation that destroy long-term signal fidelity; (2) fundamental electrophysiological noise floors (≈ 1–10 µV/√Hz) that obscure sub-cellular synaptic action potentials and picotesla biomagnetic fields; and (3) pervasive data-harvesting vulnerabilities, wherein raw neurological telemetry and somatic signatures are transmitted across unencrypted wireless links, exposing cognitive privacy and biometric identity to commercial artificial intelligence harvesting and unauthorized foundation-model distillation. This monograph establishes the theoretical formulation, physical-layer engineering, and cryptographic governance architecture for Bio-Integrated Quantum Diamond Sensors (BQDS): (1) We model optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) in nitrogen-vacancy (NV^-) centers embedded in surface-functionalized nanodiamonds and flexible lithium niobate (LiNbO3) phononic substrates, achieving a magnetic sensitivity floor of η_B ≤ 8.5 pT/√Hz at physiological temperature (T ≈ 310 K); (2) We derive non-Markovian vibronic shielding equations demonstrating that bio-compatible acoustic superlattices filter out destructive thermal phonon modes, extending ground-state electron spin coherence to T_2^* ≥ 1.45 µs and spin-lattice relaxation to T_1 ≥ 4.8 ms; (3) We construct the Somatic Cryptographic Interlock (SCI), which transduces chaotic micro-variations in cardiac intervals and axonal firing sequences directly into true quantum random bitstreams (H_∞ ≥ 0.992 bits/bit), generating on-chip zero-knowledge authentication proofs without disclosing raw physiological waveforms; and (4) We formulate an autonomous bio-hardware circuit breaker that optically decouples wireless transceivers in under 12 ns upon detecting unauthorized interrogation or electromagnetic probing. We prove that this architecture guarantees cognitive privacy under GDPR Article 9 while enforcing director fiduciary obligations under Delaware Caremark corporate governance.

title: Legal Challenges In International Commercial Payments With Special Reference To Letters Of Credit In The Digital Economy
summary: International commercial payments make the world go round, and Letters of Credit (LCs) are at the heart of it all, trusted by buyers and sellers everywhere. They’ve been the gold standard for minimizing risk in global trade, mostly thanks to the rules laid out in UCP 600. But times are changing fast. As trade moves online, we’re seeing everything shift: electronic documents, blockchain, fintech apps, digital banks. These new tools are great, but they’re also bringing a whole bunch of legal headaches, think questions about how to validate electronic documents, worries about authentication, cybersecurity, privacy, fraud, cross-border disputes, and keeping up with a patchwork of regulations. This study dives into the legal maze surrounding Letters of Credit in today’s digital economy, focusing on how international payments work now. It takes a hard look at big legal frameworks like UCP 600 and the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records (MLETR), plus Indian laws such as the Information Technology Act, FEMA, and various banking rules. The research spots some pretty serious gaps, showing that the current laws aren’t quite keeping pace with new digital risks. In the end, it calls for smarter regulations and fresh policies, so we can better control digital LCs, resolve legal uncertainties across borders, and make international trade safer, faster, and more reliable. All that, with the goal of protecting the integrity of global payments, even as technology keeps changing the game.
